policy.criticalRule: Cybersecurity and robotics stages include mandatory safety/authorization items; a stage cannot receive prior-knowledge credit when one of those critical items is wrong.
policy.unlockRule: Credit only consecutive mastered stages. Keep credited stages open for review, enable the first unmet stage as the active Theory + Workshop stage, and lock later stages.

stages.title: Web foundations & DOM
stages.focus: Understand structure, presentation and event-driven browser behavior.
theory: HTML defines semantic structure; CSS defines presentation.
The DOM is the browser's programmable representation of the document.
Events connect user actions such as clicks/submits to JavaScript behavior.
workshop: Build a semantic interface shell.
Handle one DOM event without inline duplicated logic.
Explain HTML vs CSS vs DOM/event responsibilities.
stages.evidence: Semantic page + one working event flow.

stages.title: Validation & browser persistence
stages.focus: Protect inputs and preserve small project state.
theory: Validate type/range before using or storing input.
localStorage is appropriate for small browser-only prototypes.
Persist structured data by serializing and reconstructing it.
workshop: Validate a numeric or categorical input.
Persist a small collection with JSON + localStorage.
Reload and prove the same state is recovered.

stages.title: Async flow, debugging & accessibility
stages.focus: Handle asynchronous behavior and make the interface inspectable and usable.
theory: fetch is asynchronous and failures must be handled explicitly.
Debugging starts by inspecting the value and point where it is produced.
Labels, semantics and keyboard-friendly interaction improve accessibility.
workshop: Trace one async or delayed flow.
Diagnose one controlled undefined/error case.
Run a labels/semantics/keyboard accessibility check.

stages.title: Git, safe rendering & OOP architecture
stages.focus: Make the project versioned, safer to render and organized by responsibility.
theory: A commit is an identifiable project change.
User input should be treated as text/validated for its rendering context rather than inserted blindly as HTML.
OOP separates domain responsibilities from the interface.
workshop: Create one meaningful commit with a focused change.
Render user-provided text without blind HTML injection.
Model one domain class and synchronize it with UML.

stages.title: Dataset & Python foundations
stages.focus: Represent observations and variables with basic Python structures.
theory: Columns represent variables; rows represent observations.
Lists preserve ordered collections of values.
CSV provides a tabular text format that can be loaded into analysis tools.
workshop: Represent a tiny dataset in Python.
Identify rows, columns and variable types.
Load or parse a small CSV sample.

stages.title: Robust summaries & data quality
stages.focus: Choose summaries carefully and reason about missingness and association.
theory: Median is more resistant than mean to extreme values.
Missing values require context-aware treatment.
Correlation indicates association, not proof of causation.
workshop: Compare mean and median on a skewed sample.
Identify missing values and justify a treatment.
Explain one correlation without causal overclaim.

stages.title: Outliers, distributions & Pandas
stages.focus: Inspect unusual values and use tabular tools to understand distributions.
theory: An outlier should be investigated before automatic removal.
Histograms help inspect the distribution of numerical data.
A DataFrame is a labeled tabular structure for data operations.
workshop: Inspect one unusual value and classify its possible cause.
Create a distribution plot.
Use a DataFrame to inspect/filter the dataset.
stages.evidence: Outlier note + distribution visual + DataFrame operation.

stages.title: Reproducibility, visualization & OOP pipeline
stages.focus: Make analysis rerunnable, interpretable and architecturally clear.
theory: A reproducible notebook/script records the path from input to result.
Charts need meaningful titles, labels and units.
Dataset/Cleaner/Analyzer/Report is an example of separated responsibilities.
workshop: Run the analysis from a clean start.
Improve one visualization's labels/context.
Model the analysis pipeline with classes/functions and UML.

tracks.title: Defensive Cybersecurity
tracks.safety: Authorized defensive scope only. No external target exploitation, credential theft, persistence, malware or destructive testing.

stages.title: Security foundations & authorized scope
stages.focus: Establish CIA, least privilege and the boundary of permitted defensive work.
theory: CIA means confidentiality, integrity and availability.
Least privilege gives only the permissions required for a role.
Testing is limited to owned, sandboxed or explicitly authorized systems.
workshop: Identify confidentiality/integrity/availability needs for the simulated app.
Write an authorized-scope statement with explicit exclusions.
Create a least-privilege role example.
stages.evidence: CIA map + authorized scope + role boundary.

stages.title: Identity, validation & protected operations
stages.focus: Separate authentication from authorization and validate untrusted inputs.
theory: Authentication verifies identity; authorization decides allowed actions.
Validate format/range before processing external input.
Protected operations must check session/identity and permissions in a trusted component.
workshop: Model User/Role/Session responsibilities.
Create an allow-list validator for a safe form.
Simulate one allowed and one denied protected operation.
stages.evidence: Identity model + validator + access decision evidence.

stages.title: Audit, credential protection & secrets
stages.focus: Preserve useful evidence without leaking sensitive values.
theory: Audit logs record relevant events and context, not plaintext passwords.
Real passwords require appropriate password hashing with salt.
Private/service-role keys and other secrets never belong in public repos or browser code.
workshop: Design a minimal audit-event schema.
Review a mock credential-storage choice and correct it.
Run a repository secret-exposure checklist on a safe sample.
stages.evidence: Audit schema + credential rule + secret checklist.

stages.title: Threat model, safe errors & OOP security architecture
stages.focus: Reason about threats and organize defensive controls without exposing internals.
theory: Threat models connect assets, threats, trust boundaries and mitigations.
Errors should be useful without exposing unnecessary sensitive detail.
User/Role/Session/Validator/AuditLog can separate defensive responsibilities.
workshop: Create a compact threat model for the simulated project.
Compare safe and over-detailed error messages.
Build/update UML for the defensive services and state one residual risk.
stages.evidence: Threat model + safe-error review + security UML.

stages.title: Coordinates, parameters & primitives
stages.focus: Define reproducible geometry from coordinates and parameters.
theory: 3D points use x, y and z coordinates.
Parametric geometry changes from explicit dimensions/parameters.
Primitives such as cubes and cylinders are reusable building blocks.
workshop: Define origin/axes for the model.
Create one parametric primitive.
Change one parameter and compare results.

stages.title: Translation, scale & rotation
stages.focus: Transform geometry predictably.
theory: Translation changes position.
Scale changes size relative to a defined factor/reference.
Rotation requires an axis/pivot and angle.
workshop: Translate one object.
Scale a copy by a documented factor.
Rotate around a defined axis and record the result.

stages.title: Extrusion, validation & units
stages.focus: Generate valid solids while preserving dimensional meaning.
theory: Extrusion produces volume by extending a 2D profile.
Impossible dimensions such as negative thickness must be rejected/handled explicitly.
Consistent units prevent scale errors.
workshop: Extrude a simple profile.
Reject one invalid dimension.
Document and verify the project's unit convention.
stages.evidence: Extruded solid + validation case + unit sheet.

stages.title: Export, composition & OOP architecture
stages.focus: Combine parts and deliver a coherent parametric system.
theory: Export formats such as STL are used for downstream 3D workflows.
Composition builds a larger object from related parts.
Shape/Solid/Transform/Assembly separates responsibilities in an OOP model.
workshop: Export a validated model with documented scale.
Compose an assembly from reusable parts.
Draw synchronized UML for the geometry architecture.

tracks.title: Robotics & Automation
tracks.safety: Simulate first. With hardware, respect electrical ratings, mechanical limits, safe states and teacher-approved connections.

stages.title: Sensors, actuators & I/O flow
stages.focus: Identify what the system senses, decides and controls.
theory: Sensors measure/detect system conditions.
Actuators produce controlled physical outputs.
Automation can be modeled as input → control/decision → output.
workshop: Create an I/O table.
Classify each device as sensor/actuator/controller interface.
Define expected units/ranges for inputs and outputs.

stages.title: State machines, validation & fail-safe
stages.focus: Define deterministic transitions and a safe response to invalid readings.
theory: State machines define states and allowed transitions.
Impossible sensor readings must be detected rather than used blindly.
Fail-safe means a defined safer state/behavior when assumptions fail.
workshop: Draw a state machine with at least three states.
Add an invalid-reading transition.
Define the actuator outputs for the safe state.

stages.title: Digital control, PWM & simulation
stages.focus: Understand discrete control and test logic before hardware.
theory: Digital signals represent discrete states such as LOW/HIGH.
PWM approximates controllable power/brightness/speed through duty cycle.
Simulation makes control tests repeatable with lower hardware risk.
workshop: Model a LOW/HIGH input decision.
Simulate two PWM duty-cycle cases.
Run a sensor/decision/output sequence before physical integration.

stages.title: Debugging, hardware limits & OOP architecture
stages.focus: Integrate safely with observable state and separated controller responsibilities.
theory: Useful control logs include input, current state, decision and output.
Hardware integration must respect voltage/current/polarity and device limits.
Sensor/Controller/Actuator/System separates responsibilities and supports simulation.
workshop: Create a debugging trace for one failure.
Complete a teacher-approved hardware safety checklist or advanced simulation equivalent.
Model Sensor/Controller/Actuator/System in UML and run one integration test.
stages.evidence: Debug trace + safety checklist + controller UML.
